calls.reason: The Chollet et al. report shows preparatory ARC training was established practice, but no reliable transcript or slide record of the video was recovered, so its disclosure cannot be judged.
ARC's own evaluator, Chollet, said on Dec 20 that o3 was not AGI and still failed very easy tasks. Independent analysis found 34 of 400 tasks unsolved. No evidence suggests broad human-level ability.
The MIT paper confirms a strong prior result of 61.9% on public validation, but OpenAI's graph was never recovered, so the omission and the halfway placement cannot be checked.
Evidence is mixed: pooled human studies suggest humans can solve nearly all tasks, but a live blog reports Kamradt saying o3 beat the top human result. No matched individual-human comparison exists.
ARC Prize's December report lists prior results such as MARA(BARC)+MIT, but neither original graph was recovered, so the omissions and framing are unverified.
ARC Prize later confirmed o3-preview was trained on 75% of ARC-AGI-1, but no record shows whether an ARC-untrained version was ever evaluated internally.
